title: How EasyGen drives ~18% of revenue via affiliates, led by employees and customers
summary: Ruben explains how EasyGen, a bootstrapped LinkedIn post generator, gets about 18% of its roughly $50K MRR from affiliates, with most of it coming from four people. He covers turning employees into affiliates, coupon-based tracking, community building around one problem, and refusing automation and VC money.

principles.text: Concentrate affiliate bets on a few people, and make some of them your team: they get equity-like upside on top of salary.
principles.quote: 80% of that money it's just four people and out of those four people two of them are my employees so I'm paying them affiliate deals through re food

principles.text: Use coupon codes instead of links to track affiliates: buyers can see the discount applied, so it feels sturdier.
principles.quote: if they click on the link they're afraid it's not working if you use a coupon you can see on stripe the you know like the numbers

principles.text: Be the heaviest user of your own product; affiliates credible with it are your best sellers, so recruit from customers first.
principles.quote: I made sure that I'm the most prominent user of e gen no one used EAS gen more than me and I think it's a good thing as a Founder to be the guy who used the product the most

principles.text: Build community with realistic expectations: aim for about one engaged person a day by solving one specific problem.
principles.quote: you should aim at 1,000 people over three years 1,000 people over three years is 300 people per year that's 10 people per month

principles.text: Never automate posting: platforms hunt bot-like behavior, so keep a human on the platform.
principles.quote: if you behave like a bot well it turns out that social media have insanely big teams and their only sole purpose is to find people who behave like Bots

principles.text: Stay bootstrapped to keep ownership, speed and fun over a bigger but VC-constrained outcome.
principles.quote: I'd rather have a business that is making 100K a month um where I own 80% of the company and have a lot of fun doing it than one that is making 10 Millions a month
